description: Make the host detect and refuse to silently use degraded CSI, and keep raw data from calibration runs so they can be analysed offline. Today the app accepted a calibration where walking was indistinguishable from the empty room (separable=false) and applied it, and no raw CSI was kept. Add (1) a CSI resolution diagnostic (raw amplitude level and fraction of zero values) per frame and in /api/status with a clear warning, (2) calibration warnings plus an explicit 'save anyway' confirmation when motion is not separable or resolution is low, (3) automatic raw CSI recording of each calibration step into data/recordings, and (4) an offline `diagnose` CLI that replays recorded takes through the real pipeline and prints per-take resolution, motion-score and posture statistics. Depends on FEAT-001 only; independent of FEAT-002.
steps: backend/processing.py: per packet, in addition to mean_amp, keep the median raw amplitude and the fraction of valid subcarriers whose raw amplitude is exactly 0 (store in _Entry). In compute_frame aggregate over the window into new MotionFrame fields `raw_amplitude_median` and `raw_zero_fraction` (Optional[float]) and `low_resolution` (bool). Module constants: LOW_RES_MEDIAN_AMP (e.g. 4.0 raw units) and LOW_RES_ZERO_FRACTION (e.g. 0.15); low_resolution = median < LOW_RES_MEDIAN_AMP or zero_fraction > LOW_RES_ZERO_FRACTION. This is a warning, NOT a quality gate: quality_ok and quality_reasons must not change. Update the module docstring. Check that frame.to_dict() and existing tests still work.

backend/engine.py snapshot(): add `csi_resolution` {median_amplitude, zero_fraction, low, message} from the last frame. message when low: CSI values are only about N units with X% zeros, so the signal is quantised and moving/still and sitting/standing detection will be unreliable; reflash the receiver with the current firmware (gain compensation off, see firmware/README.md) or press reset on the receiver board, then recalibrate. Dashboard: show this as a visible warning on the Sensor page and on the Calibrate page (dashboard/static/app.js, index.html, style.css; follow existing warning/banner patterns and CSP).

backend/calibration.py: StepData accumulates the per-frame raw_amplitude_median / raw_zero_fraction of good frames; compute_calibration adds a `csi_resolution` block (median of medians, mean zero fraction, low flag) and a warning when low, and a top-level `needs_confirmation` list of reasons (non-separable motion, low resolution). CalibrationManager.save() (and the POST /api/calibration/save route in dashboard/server.py) must raise CalibrationError with a clear message when needs_confirmation is non-empty unless the body has `"confirm": true`; the Calibrate page shows the reasons and a 'Save anyway' button that resends with confirm. Saved files keep needs_confirmation for later inspection. Existing calibration files (format 2, without these keys) must still load.

Raw CSI recording of calibration runs: when a run starts on a live (non-synthetic) source, the CalibrationManager records each step's raw lines as a take using the existing backend/recording.py RecordingManager (dashboard/server.py constructs both; pass the recording manager into CalibrationManager, optional so tests without it still work). Create a session with placement '<placement>-calibration' and notes 'calibration run <iso time>', and for each step start a take when the step starts recording and stop it when the step finishes or fails (label map: empty_baseline->empty_room, walking->walking, standing_still->standing_still, sitting->sitting). Do not start if a user take is already running (warn instead). Recording failures add a warning but never fail the calibration. Store {session_id, takes: {step_key: take_id}} as `raw_recording` in the calibration result and expose it in /api/calibration/state. Mind threading: step transitions happen in the engine thread (CalibrationSession.add_frame / tick) and from HTTP handlers; RecordingManager writes in the engine thread; reuse the managers' locks, avoid deadlocks, and add a test.

Offline diagnosis: add `diagnose` to backend/cli.py: `python -m backend.cli diagnose --session data/recordings/<id> [--calibration data/calibration/<key>.json]` and `--file <take.csv>` (TAKE_FIELDS CSV). Replay each take through SignalProcessor with the same config (reuse backend/offline.py OfflineReplay / apply_calibration_file), and print per take: label, packets, packet rate, raw amplitude median / zero fraction / low_resolution, motion_score median/p75/p95/max, fraction of frames above the calibration's movement threshold, and, when the calibration has a posture model, the distribution of PostureClassifier raw labels. Also print a summary line comparing walking vs quiet takes (median vs p95, the same separability rule as compute_calibration). Add `make diagnose SESSION=... [CAL=...]` to the Makefile (and its help comment line).

Real-data fixture: create tests/fixtures/quantised_csi_excerpt.csv with the first ~300 data rows (plus header) of .agents/tasks/task-csi-resolution-walking-fix/diag_capture_20261024-185452.csv (real ESP32-S3 capture with 0-3 LSB CSI). Tests: tests/test_processing.py (the excerpt replayed through SignalProcessor yields low_resolution True with zero_fraction > 0.2; synthetic csi_synth packets with normal amplitudes yield low_resolution False; quality_ok unaffected); tests/test_calibration.py (needs_confirmation populated for a non-separable synthetic run; save without confirm raises, with confirm saves; old-format file loads); a recording test for calibration takes (steps produce takes with the mapped labels in a temp SessionStore); tests/test_cli.py or a new test for `diagnose` on the fixture (exit code 0, output mentions low resolution); dashboard/API test for save confirm and csi_resolution in /api/status.

After implementing, run the diagnose CLI on the full capture: `.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli diagnose --file .agents/tasks/task-csi-resolution-walking-fix/diag_capture_20261024-185452.csv --calibration data/calibration/office__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128.json` and paste the output into findings.

Remove the empty leftover directory data/recordings/20261024-185452-diagnostic/ (it only holds a session.json whose take was deleted). README.md: document the resolution warning, the save confirmation, the automatic raw recording of calibration steps (where it goes, that it is local only), and `make diagnose`.
acceptance_criteria: /api/status contains csi_resolution and reports low=true for the real quantised excerpt replayed through the engine/processor, low=false for normal synthetic data
A calibration with separable=false or low resolution cannot be saved without confirm=true; the UI offers 'Save anyway' and lists the reasons
A live calibration run writes one take per step under data/recordings/<session>/ with labels empty_room/walking/standing_still/sitting, referenced from the calibration result
`python -m backend.cli diagnose` works on a session directory and on a single take CSV and its output for the real capture is recorded in findings
make test passes with the new tests
